topic: The Triangle of Power: A Unified Notation for Powers, Roots, and Logarithms
target_audience: High school students and math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
sections.content: Introduce the three mathematical 'siblings' that belong together but use confusingly different notations: Exponents (3²=9), Roots (√9=3), and Logarithms (log₃9=2). Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Lion', trying to solve three different puzzles that are actually the same shape.
sections.example: Leo sees 2³=8, ∛8=2, and log₂8=3 as three separate languages. We need a 'Universal Translator'.

sections.title: Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars
sections.content: Briefly review the roles of the Base (the multiplier), the Exponent (how many times), and the Result (the total value). Use a simple 2x2x2 block visual to show how 2³ leads to 8.
sections.example: Base: 2, Exponent: 3, Result: 8. These are the three vertices of our upcoming triangle.

sections.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
sections.content: Construct a single geometric shape (an equilateral triangle) to replace all three notations. Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex, the Exponent at the top vertex, and the Result at the bottom-right vertex. Explain that the relationship remains fixed regardless of which value is missing.
sections.example: A triangle with '3' on the bottom-left, '2' at the peak, and '9' on the bottom-right represents the complete relationship: 3²=9.

sections.title: Operation 1: The Power (Top-Down View)
sections.content: Demonstrate how to find the 'Result' when the bottom-left (Base) and top (Exponent) are known. Visually, the 'power' flows from the base up through the exponent to reach the result.
sections.example: Input: Base 5, Exponent 2. Visual: The triangle fills from the left and top to reveal '25' at the bottom-right. (5² = 25)

sections.title: Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)
sections.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Base' when the Result and Exponent are known. In the triangle, this looks like tracing the bottom edge backwards from the right corner. This unifies the 'radical' concept into the triangle structure.
sections.example: Input: Result 64, Exponent 3. Visual: A question mark appears at the Base vertex. Solving it reveals '4' because 4³ = 64.

sections.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
sections.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Exponent' when the Base and Result are known. This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking 'to what height' must the base grow to reach the result.
sections.example: Input: Base 10, Result 1000. Visual: The 'top' vertex is missing. We find it is '3' because 10³ = 1000. This replaces 'log₁₀1000 = 3'.

sections.title: Summary: The Unified Harmony
sections.content: A final animation showing the Triangle of Power rotating, with Leo the Lion easily switching between finding bases, exponents, and results using just one mental map. Emphasize that math is about relationships, not just symbols.
sections.example: The triangle glows, and the symbols √, log, and ^ merge into the single triangular shape, simplifying the student's cognitive load.
